Plugin Studio apps

Build a small application — a form, a diagram of steps over data stores, APIs, databases and scripts, and an output with actions — and publish it as its own entry in Operations → Plugins for the ADOMs and the groups or people you pick.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced userOperator
🔑 Permissionsstudio.script_library
📍 WhereAuthor — Plugin Studio (first level of the sidebar) → Apps (URL /studio/ and /studio/apps/<id>). User — Operations → Plugins → <app> (in Global, Global → Plugins; URL /apps/<id>)

What is it?#

An app is something an administrator builds in Plugin Studio for other people to use: a form they fill in, a diagram of steps that does the work, and an output they see, with actions they can take on it. Once published, it is an entry of its own in Operations → Plugins — only for the ADOMs and the groups or people the administrator picked.

Every plugin is an app (since 2026-10-23). New app asks for the type: Flow — the form, diagram and output this article describes — or Script — Python code with a form, run in the sandbox, written in the Script Library editor. Both kinds are listed together in Plugin Studio → Apps, with the same actions, and both appear under Plugins.

The Apps list and its actions#

Action What it does
Edit Opens the editor (a script app opens the script editor)
Disable / Enable A disabled app leaves every menu and starts no run: an operator run, an automation on a trigger, Run another app, a Run a script step, a saved script schedule (skipped, not paused). Nothing is deleted; an author can still test the draft.
Download data A zip with app.json, the runs and a CSV per data store the app uses
Export app package The app as a .satomplugin package (a script app: Download the code)
Reset Deletes the app's data from the database: its runs and every row of the data stores only it uses. Shared stores keep their rows and are listed in the answer. Design, versions, connections and settings stay. Refused while a run is in progress.
Delete Deletes the app for good, with its runs and the data stores only it uses (a script app: the script, its versions, saved runs, run records and credentials). Connections and APIs are kept. Refused for a template and for an app another app runs.

Reset and Delete ask you to type the app id. Templates — what Examples installs — carry a Template badge and have no Delete: they can be edited, disabled, reset and downloaded, never deleted, and every delete route (app, script, data store, connection) refuses them.

What does it do?#

The form — text, textarea, number, date, checkbox and password fields, and four kinds of list: fixed choices, the values of a data store column, a list read from an API through a connection, or a SATOM list — FortiWeb appliances, the FortiWebs' server pools, interfaces and local certificates (local cache; each choice names the devices that have it), approved Web Protection Profile templates, usable Certificate Manager certificates, certificate providers, classification zones / lines / departments, network segments. The server re-reads the choices and refuses a value that is not one of them. Tick searchable on a list to give it a search box: every word must match, a counter shows matches / total, a choice you made stays selected while you search, and Enter in the box never runs the app.

The diagram — boxes and arrows drawn in the app editor. Steps:

Group Step What it does
Flow Start / End Where the run begins and ends
Flow Set a variable Saves a value under a name
Flow Decision Compares two values (equals, not equals, contains, greater, less, empty, not empty, true) → yes / no
Flow Fail Stops the run as failed, with a message the user sees
Flow Output Shows a value as a table, list, key/value, text or JSON
Data Read a data store The rows that match a filter
Data Write a data store Insert, update, upsert or delete rows
Data Query a database SQL against a PostgreSQL connection (read-only unless Allow writes)
Actions Call an API A request to an HTTP connection; Keep only takes a JSON path
Actions Run a script The published version of a Script Library script
SATOM Render names Object names from patterns such as spo-{extra}-{service}-{port} and vs-{spo}; an empty value takes its dash with it; a name FortiWeb would refuse is an error
SATOM DDI: reserve an address One A record (IPAM) in one DDI unit: an existing record is reused; else the next free address of the first subnet that has one, or a given address (the same IP in another unit). The record read back decides
SATOM DDI: reserve by rules One reservation per rule row in order (the master unit first); ip_from reuses another unit's address; a failure releases what the step created. Mode given: the addresses typed in the form, the DDI is not called (nothing typed is an error)
SATOM DDI: release reservations Deletes only what reserve steps of this run created
SATOM Pick a FortiWeb by capacity The first FortiWeb by name in a zone / line / department with room under its Capacity limit. Objects the device must have (requires, JSON: certificate, server_pool, interface, web_protection_profile — a template id or a name) skips a FortiWeb with room that lacks one, read on the device when it answers; an empty value does not constrain, so the form's choices pick the device. When none qualifies, the error names the limit or the missing object per FortiWeb
SATOM Certificate (issue or reuse) issue: issues with the chosen provider and deploys it; existing: deploys a Certificate Manager certificate; device: uses a local certificate already on the appliance — checked on the device, nothing written. An internal-only provider refuses a non-Internal zone
SATOM FortiWeb: create the server policy Virtual server, VIP, pool and members (or an existing pool, checked on the device first and never written), a custom service when the port is not 443/80, then the policy; a failed object deletes what the step wrote
SATOM FortiWeb: remove a created policy Deletes what a create step of this run wrote, newest first

An app started by a trigger also sees the whole event as {{ event }} (write {{ event | default({}) }} in an app that also runs by hand).

Steps read the form and earlier results through templates: {{ form.host }}, {{ rows }}, {{ rows | length }}. A value that is exactly one {{ expression }} keeps its type, so a list stays a list. An undefined name stops the step with an error — write {{ x | default('') }} for an optional one.

Arrows — a step ends ok or error, a decision yes or no. The run follows the arrow of that outcome, otherwise the always arrow — but an error follows only an error arrow; with none, the run stops there as failed. A loop stops after 200 steps, a run after 10 minutes. The error arrows are where you decide what a failure undoes: point a step's error arrow at DDI: release / FortiWeb: remove and only what this run created is undone.

Analyze and Last run — Analyze explains the diagram being edited: what each step saves and reads, where its error goes and which undo steps that path reaches, plus warnings (a step no arrow reaches, a variable no step saves, a decision with one way out, a write with no error arrow after another write). Last run colours each step by how it ended; a test run is laid over the diagram as it finishes, and clicking a step shows its detail.

Jobs — an armed run whose diagram writes is also a job (Jobs page and toast), with one log line per step: where it failed and why.

Packages — Export package writes the app with its data stores (columns and rows), its HTTP connections without secrets and their API Catalog versions as one plugin package; Import app package installs one without overwriting this server's rows, connections or secrets.

Actions on the output — buttons under a finished run: save to a data store, download CSV or JSON, send to a connection, run another app with the output, or raise a change request.

❗Important

An action never changes a device. Raise a change request creates a draft change request — with the app and the run named in it — that goes through the normal approval before anything runs. Only the SATOM steps that issue a certificate or create / remove a server policy write to an appliance, and only in an armed run, for a user who holds config_write; a rehearsal describes them.

Limits#

  • 2 runs in progress per user, 8 per node; the Run button allows 30 presses a minute; a run request over 1 MiB is refused.
  • Templates are bounded: an exponent above 64, a result longer than 1 MiB, more than 1,000,000 loop items or a rendered text over 1 MiB is refused.
  • A value put into an API path is percent-encoded, slash included, so a form value stays one path segment; pass values as query parameters with Query string (JSON).
  • A list filled from an API is fetched at most once a minute.
  • An action runs once per run (Download can be repeated), and only on the version that produced the run.
  • Users who are not authors see which steps ran and how they ended, not the step details; the message of a Fail step is shown.
  • Password values are also masked in their urlencode, tojson and base64 spellings. Run records are kept 90 days.

See Plugin Studio examples for complete apps to start from, and the Studio security model.

The look: Design#

The Design tab lays out two surfaces, switched with Page / Result:

Surface What you place Other blocks
Page Each form field, the Run button, the result area, the app description, the recent runs Section, Card, Columns (1–4, widths out of 12), Tabs, Banner, Heading, Text (Markdown), Callout, Image, Link button, Divider, Spacer
Result The run status, each Output step (title and Show as can be overridden, with or without a card), number tiles (a value inside an output; a list counts its items), the action buttons, the steps, Other outputs The same layout and content blocks

Drag blocks from the palette onto the canvas (or click one: it goes into the selected card, column or tab, or after the selected block); drag blocks to move them; select them on the canvas or in the Outline (up, down, duplicate, delete; Delete, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y). Every block has a style: background (two colours make a gradient), text and border colour — any hex colour — and preset padding, space below, corners, shadow, border, text size, weight, alignment and width. With nothing selected the inspector edits the theme: accent, page background, text, card surface, borders, corners and page padding, applied inside the app only. Images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP; up to 512 KiB, 12 per app; no SVG) are uploaded to the app. As users see it shows the real page, and the result filled with the newest run. Start from the standard layout turns the usual layout into blocks; Clear returns to it. Save design, then Publish: users see a design only once it is published.

  • SATOM draws every block with its own styles; a design recolours and spaces them. There is no HTML or CSS of your own (text is Markdown without raw HTML), so an app cannot run code in SATOM or read what a user types.
  • A field the page leaves out is added before the Run button, and a missing Run button, result area, status, outputs, actions or steps are added at the end — nothing a user needs is lost.
  • Publish is refused while a field is placed twice or a block names a field, Output step or image that is not there. Hard-to-read colours (contrast under 4.5:1) are only warned about.
  • The design and its images travel in the app package.

Requirements#

  • Published Script Library scripts for Run a script steps, and satom-scripts.path running on the node.
  • Data stores and connections for the steps that use them.

Permissions#

Action Permission
Build, test, publish and delete apps studio.script_library
Use an app (its menu entry, its runs, its actions) Be in its access list: one of its groups or people — no permission key
Manage groups (Administrator → Access → Groups) users.manage

Nobody outside the access list sees the menu entry; opening the app, its runs or their actions answers not found. Each user sees their own runs; authors see all runs and their variables.

How to use#

Build an app#

  1. Plugin Studio (first level of the sidebar) → Apps → New app.
  2. Settings: the name and icon of the menu entry, the description, the ADOMs it appears in, and who may use it (groups and people). Save settings.
  3. Form: add the fields. Save form.
  4. Diagram: add steps from the palette, Connect them, set each step in the panel on the right. Save diagram.
  5. Actions: add the buttons the output should offer. Save actions. Design (optional): lay out the page and the result, colour them. Save design.
  6. Test: run the saved draft. Rehearsal (on by default) describes the steps that write instead of running them.
  7. Publish: the tab lists what must be fixed first; Publish freezes the draft as a new version and adds the menu entry.

Run an app from another system (API)#

An outside system runs an app through POST /api/v1/apps/<slug>/run with an API token that was granted this app (Administrator → API Tokens → Apps it may run). The grant is bound to the published version: when you publish different fields, steps or actions, the grant pauses until an administrator re-approves it on the token, so editing an app never widens what a credential outside the console can do. Publishing the same content again keeps it. The run from the API is unarmed unless the caller sends "armed": true (capability app_arm): write steps show rehearsal: not executed. Only apps the token's owner may open in its ADOM are offered; script apps run from their own page only. Deleting the app removes its grants. See REST API.

Use an app#

  1. Open it from Operations → Plugins (in Global, Global → Plugins).
  2. Fill in the form and press Run. The result appears when the run ends.
  3. Press an action button under the output.

Runbooks#

An app can carry a whole procedure — the restart activities of an appliance that is down — as automatic as the steps allow:

  • Load an appliance reads a device from the inventory ({{ form.appliance }}, or {{ event.appliance_id }} when a trigger started the run) and saves it as {{ appliance }} (host, port, ssh_port, name, kind, model, hw_type, firmware…). The form field SATOM list → Appliances (every product) offers every device.
  • Checks answer yes or no: HTTP check (status 0 = any answer), TCP check (also the runbook's "ping": SATOM cannot send ICMP), Console read (one read-only command over SSH, sent exactly as written), Appliance fact (an inventory field, e.g. hw_type = vm, without contacting the device), Collect diagnostics (the product's battery, saved under Diagnose › Log Collection). When SATOM could not look — SSH refused, no appliance, a target the guard refuses, a fact it does not know — the step takes its error arrow, never no.
  • Ask a person stops the run (waiting). The run page shows the question, the step's Instructions, Responsible and Estimated time, and the step's own buttons (Ja / Nein, or one button such as Erledigt). The person who started the run or a Plugin Studio author answers, even hours later; the run continues along that arrow with everything it had saved.
  • Activity is a documented box that passes at once (a heading such as 1 Connectivity tests). Every step has Instructions, Responsible and Estimated time.
  • Simulate (Diagram tab) walks the saved draft as a rehearsal: nothing is written to a device, the checks really look, each question stops in the panel for your answer — or tick Answer Yes to every question — and the path is coloured on the diagram.

Example#

Register a host and list them. Form: Host (text, required). Diagram: Start → Write a data store (hosts, insert, Values {"host": "{{ form.host }}"}) → Read a data store (hosts, save as rows) → Output ({{ rows }}, table) → End. Action: Download (CSV, {{ outputs[0].value }}). Share it with the group NetOps in the FortiWeb ADOM and publish.

Troubleshooting#

The app is not in my menu#

It is unpublished, it is not shown in this ADOM, or you are not in its access list. Ask its author; authors see it in Plugin Studio → Apps.

"… is not defined"#

A template names a variable or form field that does not exist at that point. Check the spelling, or use | default('') for an optional value.

My design does not show#

Users see the published design: Save design, then Publish. An app with nothing on a surface uses the standard layout for it.

"the result shows output …, which is not an Output step"#

A result block names an Output step the diagram no longer has (renamed or deleted). Pick the step again in the block, or remove the block.

A run says "interrupted"#

The service restarted while it ran. Run it again.

"a rehearsal run has nothing real to act on"#

Actions are offered on real runs only. Untick Rehearsal in the Test tab, or run the published app.
